question.text: John T. Scopes was defended by this man, who had earlier successfully defended thrill killers Leopold and Loeb.
question.clue: This man, who severed ties with a railroad company to represent Eugene V. Debs, argued that two University of Chicago students were suggestible to influence byNietzsche and had them plea guilty for killing Bobby Franks.

swap.text: This word describes the illegal production and sale of liquor during Prohibition. It also applies to anything taken without permission and distributed for profit.
swap.clue: The Purple Gang in Detroit had a major influence on this industry, which imported its main product from Belle Isle and Windsor.

question.text: The Italian-American Mafia rose to prominence by selling bootleg alcohol following the passage of this policy, which outlawed the consumption and sale of alcohol.
question.clue: Carrie Nation was a staunch supporter of this cause.

swap.leadin: The end of this novel depicts a socialist rally whose speaker repeatedly claims "Chicago will be ours!"
swap.text: Name this novel that follows the life of Lithuanian immigrant Jurgis Rudkus and graphically depicts slaughterhouses in Chicago.
swap.clue: This novel about Lithuanian immigrant Jurgus Rudkis [YUR-gus RUD-kus], whose publication inspired the passage of the 1906 Pure Food and Drug Act with its depiction of the meatpacking industry.

question.text: Early in her career, Perkins was appointed Head of the Committee on Public Safety that investigated this industrial fire. Locked stairways caused the deaths of 146 garment workers in this fire.
question.answerHtml: Triangle Shirtwaist Factory Fire [accept synonyms for fire or synonyms of tragedy; accept the Triangle Shirtwaist Company Fire; or Triangle Waist Company Fire; prompt on answers mentioning Shirtwaist but not Triangle] Note to players: description NOT acceptable, specific term required
question.clue: In the ensuing trial, Max Blanck and Isaac Harris were defended by Max Steuer, who caused their acquittal by making Kate Alterman repeat her testimony many times.

swap.text: This lawyer submitted a famous brief to the Court in the case of Muller v. Oregon arguing for special treatment for women. Justice McReynolds notably refused to speak with him after he was nominated to the Court.
swap.clue: He also attacked trusts and monopolies in Other People's Money, and How the Bankers Use It.

question.leadin: He ran his last campaign from a prison cell.
question.text: Name this American socialist, who ran for president in 1900, 1904, 1908, 1912 and 1920.
question.clue: This magazine of the Brotherhood of Locomotive Firemen was edited by this man who, while a leader of the ARU, was defended by Clarence Darrow for his leadership in the Pullman Strike.

swap.text: This socialist presidential candidate ran for president five times and ran in 1920 from a prison cell. He helped to found the Industrial Workers of the World with Bill Haywood.
swap.clue: This man later helped found a political party on whose ticket he ran five times.

question.leadin: Name these Chief Justices of the Supreme Court from some decisions they wrote.
question.text: Schecter Poultry v. U.S., Ashwander v. Tennessee Valley Authority, Norris v. Alabama
question.clue: He replaced Bainbridge Colby as Secretary of State and chaired the Washington Naval Conference.

swap.leadin: This man advocated for the entry of blacks into labor unions in his journal, The Messenger.
swap.text: Name this early civil rights leader who founded the Brotherhood of Sleeping Car Porters.
swap.clue: While at City College and with the help of Chandler Owen he founded the radical magazine that he used as his bully pulpit.

question.leadin: Answer the following about a particular piece of legislation.
question.text: This 1913 legislation lowered the rates from the earlier Payne-Aldrich Tariff and called for a federal income tax.

swap.text: This co-founder of the IWW had been a leader of the Western Federation of Miners and an urn with half of his ashes in it was buried in the Kremlin upon his 1928 death.
swap.clue: The Lawrence strike caused a split in the Socialist Party between Victor Berger's moderate faction and the radical militant faction led by this man, who later emigrated to the Soviet Union.

question.text: Supporters of this anarchist put a bomb under Palmer's porch and were alleged to have committed the 1920 Wall Street Bombing. This man founded and edited the newspaper The Subversive Chronicle.
question.clue: This associate of Mike Boda formed a group that committed the crime that led to the arrest of Andrea Salsedo, who died from falling out of a window on 15 Park Row in New York.

swap.text: After being reelected to the House of Representatives, Victor Berger was denied his seat when he was convicted under this act. The phrase "clear and present danger" originated in a case regarding this act.
swap.clue: This 1917 legislation that Daniel Ellsberg was accused of violating for stealing and leaking the Pentagon Papers.

question.leadin: When he was shot, this man told police "you stick to your trade, I'll stick to mine" and refused to name his killer.
question.text: Name this Jewish-American mobster known as the "Brain." He helped fix the 1919 World Series, was the inspiration for Meyer Wolfsheim in The Great Gatsby, and may have been killed by Dutch Schultz.
question.clue: The alleged mastermind behind the fix was this Jewish mobster and bootlegger who mentored Lucky Luciano and was killed in New York City in 1928 over poker debts.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the Chinese American women's rights activist Mabel Ping-Hua Lee.
swap.text: Before becoming a minister, Lee advocated for women's rights with NAWSA, which was led by this suffragist after Susan B. Anthony. This woman, who criticized Alice Paul, founded the League of Women Voters.
swap.clue: This future founder of the League of Women Voters was involved in planning the Golden Lane and was the leader of the largest women's suffrage organization when the Nineteenth Amendment passed.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about the somewhat lackluster presidency of Warren G. Harding.
question.text: One Harding bright spot was this act, which funded a system of prenatal and child health clinics in one of the first American welfare programs. It was spearheaded by the first woman to head a federal bureau, Julia Lathrop.
question.answerHtml: Sheppard-Towner Act [or Promotion of the Welfare and Hygiene of Maternity and Infancy Act]
question.clue: Rankin supported this progressive 1921 act, named for a couple of senators from Texas and Iowa, which provided federal money to states for maternity and child care. It was administered by the Children's Bureau of the Department of Labor.

swap.leadin: Entomological illustrator Anna Comstock became a leader of this pedagogical movement after her "handbook" of the same name became a surprise standard science textbook for the first few decades of the 20th century.
swap.text: Name this pedagogical movement that attempted to reconcile scientific knowledge with personal, emotional connections with the environment and de-emphasized book learning in favor of encounters with tangible objects. It was championed by Louis Agassiz and Liberty Hyde Bailey.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about the most ineffectual of foreign policies, Dollar Diplomacy, FTPE.
question.text: Much of the formulation of the policy was done by this Secretary of State under Taft. He also notably prosecuted some trusts as Attorney General under Teddy Roosevelt.
question.clue: This future Cabinet member defended the South Fork Fishing and Hunting Club in lawsuits blaming it for the dam's failure. He's best known for serving as William Howard Taft's pro-dollar diplomacy Secretary of State.

swap.leadin: Name these things about the policy of "dollar diplomacy," FTP each.
swap.text: The policy's strongest practitioner was this man, who resigned as a senator from Pennsylvania in 1909 to become William Howard Taft's secretary of state.
swap.clue: When William Howard Taft tried to appoint this man Secretary of State, he was briefly considered ineligible because he had served in Congress when it voted a pay raise for the position. He was confirmed after the first "Saxbe fix" temporarily lowered his salary to the pre-raise level.
